records.wording: What recent decision needed a better understanding of payroll needs or how payroll decisions are made? What was your involvement?
records.optional_probes: For supplier/HCM/consulting/investment roles, establish the product, commercial, client or strategy decision. For an employer-side use, ask about the actual payroll decision. Do not assume either route or a missing solution.

records.wording: How did you obtain the information or insight you used, and what was useful or missing?
records.optional_probes: Actual internal work, public sources and past research/service purchases where relevant. No need for confidential plans, exact budgets, personal staff names or client data.

records.wording: Looking at this proposed research offer, which parts, if any, would help that decision? What duplicates something you already have?
records.optional_probes: Show only the relevant research-only concept after B01/B02. Record the version shown, use and overlap. Show an event alternative later to distinguish its incremental value.

records.wording: What evidence and context would you need to trust and use those outputs?
records.optional_probes: Case relevance, role, geography, period, method, gaps and small qualitative sample limits. Intended output may be unachievable; retain that signal. Do not present an index, benchmark or proven causal mechanism.

records.wording: How would an organisation like yours assess paying for a defined version of this?
records.optional_probes: Actual user/payer/beneficiary, approval route, intended internal/public/client use and already granted free access. Ask only relevant probes; no price anchor, full procurement map, presumed licence or promise of contacts.

records.wording: What would have to be true before a specific proposal was worth reviewing?
records.optional_probes: Next actual decision, evidence, capacity, rights, timing, objections and a permitted next step, if any. Research funding and separately defined commercial access can be combined only if actually appropriate and agreed.

records.wording: Which recent payroll decisions or challenges, if any, would make peer research useful to you?
records.optional_probes: Ask before the benefits card. Establish actual context and alternatives without requiring a recent investment case or disclosure.

records.wording: Which parts of this proposed programme would be worthwhile to you, and which would add little value?
records.optional_probes: Show member concept after M01. Explore free research, relevant peer discussion, practical follow-through and optional recognition separately. Do not imply a booked event or confirmed council place.

records.wording: Would contributing one industry question and appropriate research input be practical? If so, what question and mode would suit you?
records.optional_probes: Optional contribution; no guarantee every question becomes a study question or every topic is answered. Interest is not permission, enrolment or actual report input.

records.wording: What conditions would make the peer group useful and comfortable?
records.optional_probes: Relevant roles, actual peer mix, provider/funder involvement, meeting mode, confidentiality, recognition and use of contributions. No names or employer-sensitive details required.

records.wording: What would make participation practical or impractical?
records.optional_probes: Time/travel, employer permission, hospitality, accessibility and preferred format only where relevant. Do not collect unnecessary personal details or promise travel/accommodation.

records.wording: If no in-person event took place, would contributing to and receiving the research still be worthwhile? What would a live discussion add?
records.optional_probes: Compare remote, written and in-person value without implying exact equivalence, capacity or annual membership. No event attendance is counted from a preference.

presentation_flow: Explain commercial feasibility purpose and unbooked concept without listing benefits.
B01/B02 before buyer concept; M01 before member benefits.
Show the relevant research-only concept first; identify wording/version and relevant use.
Ask about actual use, duplication and evidence; do not pitch every variant to every person.
Only then compare an event-supported format; record actual presentation order and what was shown.
Record objections, unknowns, conditions and permitted next step; interest is not a sale, enrolment or permission.
